claim: Construct actual maximality of the same perfect quaternion order among all module-finite Z-subrings, deriving reduced-invariant integrality rather than assuming it.

obligations.name: Same order and algebra
obligations.required_input: The PEL period lattice must not be replaced during the maximality proof.
obligations.constructed_input: All12 predecessors are byte-identical. The same B=(-210,5), μ, Rosati, perfect pairing and order basis remain fixed.
obligations.justification: All12 predecessors are byte-identical. The same B=(-210,5), μ, Rosati, perfect pairing and order basis remain fixed.

obligations.name: Noncommutative integrality boundary
obligations.required_input: Integral elements of a noncommutative ring need not be closed under arbitrary addition or multiplication.
obligations.constructed_input: Every use of IsIntegral.add and IsIntegral.mul is confined to a genuine commutative QuadraticAlgebra Q a b. Its star is an actual ring endomorphism. No commutative instance is assigned to the quaternion algebra.
obligations.justification: Every use of IsIntegral.add and IsIntegral.mul is confined to a genuine commutative QuadraticAlgebra Q a b. Its star is an actual ring endomorphism. No commutative instance is assigned to the quaternion algebra.

obligations.name: Exact quadratic carrier
obligations.required_input: A related quadratic field cannot supply invariants of the original element without comparison.
obligations.constructed_input: For the actual x, the carrier has relation ω²=−Nrd(x)+Trd(x)ω; the map sendsω to x and z to z.re+z.im*x. The original quaternion relation is checked coordinatewise.
obligations.justification: For the actual x, the carrier has relation ω²=−Nrd(x)+Trd(x)ω; the map sendsω to x and z to z.re+z.im*x. The original quaternion relation is checked coordinatewise.

obligations.name: Injectivity and exceptional scalar case
obligations.required_input: Integrality reflection requires injectivity, which fails for scalar x in a two-dimensional carrier.
obligations.constructed_input: For nonscalar x, one of its three actual imaginary coordinates is nonzero and proves the map injective. Scalar x is handled separately through the injective rational algebraMap; there is no nonscalarity assumption in the final invariant theorem.
obligations.justification: For nonscalar x, one of its three actual imaginary coordinates is nonzero and proves the map injective. Scalar x is handled separately through the injective rational algebraMap; there is no nonscalarity assumption in the final invariant theorem.

obligations.name: Integral reduced invariants
obligations.required_input: A finite overorder must supply both trace and norm integrality on its actual elements.
obligations.constructed_input: Integral x reflects to the literal quadratic generator. Conjugation, addition and multiplication there prove its trace and norm integral; injective rational scalar maps and integral closedness of Z inQ give integer values. These are exactly Trd(x),Nrd(x).
obligations.justification: Integral x reflects to the literal quadratic generator. Conjugation, addition and multiplication there prove its trace and norm integral; injective rational scalar maps and integral closedness of Z inQ give integer values. These are exactly Trd(x),Nrd(x).

obligations.name: Actual finite full lattice
obligations.required_input: A maximality statement should concern a genuine Z-order, not an arbitrary subring.
obligations.constructed_input: The exact Z⁴ additive equivalence gives Module.Finite Z order. A displayed rational linear combination of the same four basis elements spans every quaternion, with coefficients(r−j,i−5k,2j,10k).
obligations.justification: The exact Z⁴ additive equivalence gives Module.Finite Z order. A displayed rational linear combination of the same four basis elements spans every quaternion, with coefficients(r−j,i−5k,2j,10k).

obligations.name: All module-finite overorders
obligations.required_input: Trace/norm caller premises must no longer hide the maximal-order conclusion.
obligations.constructed_input: For any Subring S containingO with Module.Finite Z S, every element is integral by the actual finite-module theorem and its subtype ring map. Derived invariant integrality feeds the previously proved exact trace-dual saturation, giving S=O. The stronger elementwise-integral version is also explicit.

Derived invariant integrality feeds the previously proved exact trace-dual saturation, giving S=O. The stronger elementwise-integral version is also explicit.

obligations.name: Remaining PEL joins
obligations.required_input: A maximal order and perfect lattice are not themselves a represented PEL abelian scheme or source identification.
obligations.constructed_input: Exact local ramification classification/reduced-discriminant identification, algebraization of the period family and its universal integral moduli realization, contact-to-moduli map and Hodge/KS comparison remain separate. The genus5 contact Jacobian is not identified with the dimension2 quaternionic surface.
